subject: Operational reliability incidents and renewal path — remediation & commercial options
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@amherst.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Tim O'Neil <tim.oneil@amherst.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Production reliability incidents + renewal discussion

Jonas —

Thanks for taking this early note. Over the past week our product team observed three separate tail-latency spikes and two short outages that impacted a subset of our production traffic (US region). I’ve attached a timeline (Amherst_sla_incident_timeline.xlsx) with traces and customer-impact notes.

We’re a few months away from renewal and these incidents have put uptime and latency squarely on our execs’ radar. Specifically we need a clear remediation plan, measurable SLOs for the renewed contract, and a commercial remediation to cover the customer impact while we decide whether to expand Redwood usage.

Immediate asks:
- Can you share a short mitigation and monitoring plan that will address p95/p99 tail latency and regional failover?
- What options do you have for an accelerated premium/onramp (Dedicated pilot or priority routing)?
- Can you provide a draft amendment or credit structure we can share with procurement?

We’d like to get an executive call this week (Lydia + Tim + our CTO) to align on remediation and commercial next steps.

I’m looping Tim from procurement for timing.

Thanks,
Lydia Park
VP Ops, Amherst Analytics

Attachment: Amherst_sla_incident_timeline.xlsx (Excel, 85KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@amherst.ai>
Cc: Tim O'Neil <tim.oneil@amherst.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 12:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production reliability incidents + renewal discussion

Hi Lydia — and Tim,

I’m really sorry to hear about the recent impact; thanks for sending the timeline. I reviewed the spreadsheet and the traces with our SRE lead this morning. High-level response below and we’ll put a short remediation doc together by EOD tomorrow.

Short-term mitigations we will enact immediately (next 48 hours):
- Region-level request routing fixes to reduce cold-KV-cache misses (engine change + rollout).
- Temporary lower-batch policy for critical routes to reduce intra-batch latency variance.
- Increased KV cache allocation for the models you run; observable via the console within 2 hours.

Commercial and renewal options we can propose:
1) Dedicated pilot (2x nodes) for 60 days with guaranteed traffic isolation and a service SLA (p95/p99 targets) for the pilot window.
2) Premium SLA amendment for renewal: defined p95/p99 targets, + an incident-credit payout structure and a 30% discount on pilot pricing if you elect Dedicated within renewal.

I’ve drafted a proposed amendment and included a high-level remediation timeline (will attach redwood_proposed_amendment_v2.pdf). Karhtik — can you weigh in on the commercial levers and acceptable credit range? Marissa — can you review the amendment language when I send it?

Lydia, are you available for a 30-min exec call Thursday 11/5 or Friday 11/6? If you prefer, we can add our CTO and SRE lead to go deeper on the technical plan.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production reliability incidents + renewal discussion (internal)

Jonas —

I reviewed Lydia’s timeline and your proposed commercial options. Internally I recommend we present a clear two-path offer to Amherst:

Path A (Pilot-led conversion):
- 60-day Dedicated pilot (2 nodes), Redwood covers 50% of pilot cost as a goodwill credit.
- If Amherst converts to Dedicated within 30 days of pilot close, apply an onboarding credit equal to 20% of pilot list-cost against the first 6 months of Dedicated billing.

Path B (Hosted + SLA Amendment):
- Hosted renewal with premium SLA: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 450ms (US region), plus a one-time incident credit equal to 5% of Q3 spend applied to the renewal invoice.
- 12-month commitment to lock pricing; we require a documented evaluation window for the first 90 days.

For both paths: require a joint runbook, weekly remediation sync for first 30 days after go-live, and a post-mortem review with our engineering team.

Marissa — the amendment language will need to be precise around credit triggers and measurement windows. Rishi — need your sign-off on the credit percentages (finance).

Karthik
Senior Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@amherst.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim O'Neil <tim.oneil@amherst.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:53:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production reliability incidents + renewal discussion

Thanks, Jonas and Karthik — that’s helpful. A few clarifying items from our side before the exec call:

1) Metrics: we need concrete definitions for p95 and p99 (injection points, regional partitioning, whether synthetic traffic counts). Can you confirm measurement windows and monitoring exports so we can validate?

2) Rollback and fallback: what’s the plan if a kernel/runtime change during mitigation increases error rates? We need an automated rollback policy and a clear SLA-prescribed fallback to the last-known-good model variant.

3) Credits: procurement will expect credits be express and measurable (e.g., credit amounts tied to minutes of outage or measured SLO violations over a 30-day window). A flat percent of prior-spend is unlikely to fly without SLO linkage.

I’ve attached our procurement timing doc so you can see constraints (Amherst_procurement_timing.docx). We’ll need the amendment draft to be reasonably redline-ready for procurement to circulate internally.

We can do Thursday 11/5 at 2pm PT for a 30-min call with our CTO and procurement. If you need more engineering detail we can expand the participants.

—Lydia
Lydia Park
VP Ops, Amherst Analytics
Attachment: Amherst_procurement_timing.docx (Word, 24KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@amherst.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production reliability incidents + renewal discussion — proposed SLOs and amendment

Lydia,

Appreciate the specificity — below are the confirmations and an updated commercial framing. I’ve attached the proposed amendment (redwood_proposed_amendment_v2.pdf) for procurement review and included a short measurement appendix here.

Measurement definitions (US region):
- p95: 95th percentile response time for production traffic, measured at our edge proxy, excluding synthetic monitoring. Calculation window: rolling 24-hour buckets with 7-day lookback for trend analysis.
- p99: 99th percentile response time measured identically; sustained violations are defined as p99 > 450ms across a 24-hour window.
- Error rate: request error rate measured at the API gateway, 5xx only; SLA triggers require error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 30 minutes.

Rollback/fallback:
- Any runtime/kernel rollout will use progressive canary (1% -> 10% -> 50%) with automated rollback on error-rate spike >= 0.5% or p99 degradation > 30% vs baseline.
- We’ll provide a documented fallback to the prev-variant KV cache snapshot for critical routes.

Commercial (revised):
- Hosted premium SLA: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 450ms. Incident credit model tied to measured SLO violations (credits defined in amendment).
- Dedicated pilot option: 60-day pilot; Redwood offers a one-time pilot credit equal to 50% of pilot list price. If Amherst converts to Dedicated within 30 days, apply an onboarding credit equal to 20% of first 6 months' list price.

Attachments: redwood_proposed_amendment_v2.pdf (PDF, 210KB) — contains full amendment language and the incident-credit table. I’ve also linked the deal in HubSpot for procurement reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/3421/AMH-2026-044

We’re confirmed for Thursday 11/5 2pm PT. We’ll have our CTO (SRE lead) on the call to walk the technical mitigations and the amendment language.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the detailed definitions and the amendment draft. We reviewed the SLO language and the credit table; procurement is happier with SLO-linked credits rather than a flat percent.

We’ll take the Hosted premium SLA path as our starting point while we evaluate the Dedicated pilot in parallel. Please include your engineering lead, security, and legal on the exec call so we can complete the runbook, measurement hooks, and redline the amendment.

Confirming exec call on Thursday 11/11 at 9am PT. I’ll have our CTO, procurement, and security lead join. Post-call we’ll circulate suggested redlines to your legal team.

—Lydia
